title: How a request moves through a layered system
subtitle: Entry points, boundary, services and stores
thesis: Each layer may only call the layer beneath it, so a dependency is always visible as a downward edge.

evidence.label: Architecture decision record: one-directional layer dependencies

sections.heading: How to read this
sections.summary: Read the diagram left to right: a request enters at a source, crosses one boundary, and is served by the layer it is allowed to touch.
paragraphs: Read the diagram left to right. A request enters at a source, crosses exactly one boundary, and is then served by the layer it is allowed to touch. An edge that points backwards is a defect, not a shortcut.

sections.heading: Layered dependencies
sections.summary: Four layers: entry points, a single request boundary, services, and the stores the services own.

sections.heading: Layer responsibilities
sections.summary: Entry points authenticate, the boundary validates and routes, services hold the rules, and stores hold the bytes.
paragraphs: Entry points authenticate a caller and hand the request inward. The boundary validates and routes it — and it is the only layer allowed to know that both entry points exist. Services hold the rules; stores hold the bytes.
bullets: Boundary: validates and routes, owns no domain rules
Services: own the rules, never call a sibling directly
Stores: reached only through the service that owns them

sections.heading: The governing rule
sections.summary: The decision record states the rule the diagram draws: calls travel in one direction only.

data.quote: A layer may call the layer below it, never the one beside it.

sections.heading: What this does not show
sections.summary: Deployment, scaling and failure paths are out of scope; the diagram shows dependencies, not traffic.
paragraphs: Deployment boundaries, scaling and failure paths are out of scope. The diagram shows which layer may depend on which; it deliberately says nothing about how much traffic any edge carries.

annotations.label: The only entry point
annotations.detail: Everything crosses this layer exactly once.
